newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's water stock nearly doubles in 1st qtr.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's water stock nearly doubles in 1st qtr.

text.p: Morocco's water stock nearly doubled in the first quarter of 1997 to 10.9 billion cubic metres or three years supply for the main cities and agriculture areas, the public works ministry said on Thursday.
According to official figures, water stock was around 5.0 billion cubic metres in the first quarter of 1996.

Morocco's water reservoirs were "at a level of 79.6 percent of total capacity, which represents a record stock compared with the first quarter of 1996...It will ensure three years supply for main cities and agriculture irrigated areas," the ministry said.
The country has 60 medium and large-size dams that provide water to irrigate nearly 1.0 million hectares.
Morocco, whose agriculture generates 20 percent of GDP, plans to build 40 new dams in the coming two decades to expand irrigated surfaces, officials said.

Subject to cyclical droughts since the beginning of 1990s, Morocco is trying to improve its water capacity to meet the increasing demand of both agriculture and urban households, a Moroccan water expert said.

The country, which badly needs rains for its cereal crops, expects a drop in cereals output to 3.35 million tonnes in 1996/97 season from the exceptional 10 million tonne harvest in 1995/96 due to weather changes, the agriculture ministry recently said. --Rabat newsroom 212-7 72 65 18
